The same-product OL distributor 4399 guide dated 2023-06-30 explains tied minimum/maximum, self inclusion, only one branch per preparation when both qualify, actual-phase skips and physical pile movements. observations: Minimum and maximum hand counts need not be unique; the current preparation owner may be Zhang Shiping himself.
When both the minimum and maximum conditions hold and neither branch has been used this round, choose one branch in that preparation. The two branch quotas remain separate for the round.
Skipping the matching Draw or Play phase does not create its extra phase. A real first Play phase can be followed by an extra Play phase even if that later phase is itself skipped.
The three opening mounts are placed on the general outside any actual turn. Moving one from that pile into equipment at ending is a genuine pile/equipment movement.

ruleInterpretations: One source chooses at most one branch at each actual preparation. A tied recipient qualifies. The same recipient can receive both phase types from different preparations/sources when each independent source and round quota permits; one preparation does not execute both choices.

Next Draw/Play means the next matching phase actually executed in this same actual turn, including a phase already inserted by another native phase schedule. No matching actual phase means no grant execution; promises cannot carry across actual turns.

The inserted phase is a genuine Draw/Play phase, resetting only native phase quotas. It has no new preparation, extra whole turn or invented Discard stage. Its return restores the original ending cursor, actual phase key and any suspended outer phase schedule.

Once granted, source loss or source death does not revoke a promised phase: the text binds the recipient and this turn, not continued possession. A dead beneficiary takes no further phases. These continuation details are explicit implementation inferences from issued skill effects.

XingGu selects up to three distinct physical mounts randomly without replacement from the current draw pile at game start, then stores them publicly. No entity is fabricated if the available mount count is smaller.

An accepted ending placement directly moves a real stored mount into another living character equipment area, inheriting native slot capacity, abolition and replacement rules. It is not a card use. After placement children finish, a still-living source obtains one random physical Diamond from the current draw pile; no matching Diamond means no card and no reshuffle. Completed placement survives source loss; death prevents a dead owner obtaining cards.
No current official FAQ was found overriding these timing/continuation details; explanatory product rulings and remaining implementation inferences are distinguished above.
runtimeBoundaries: All pending branch choices, public-pile placement and native child receipts live on their owning ProgramSkillFrame. Promises and quota provenance are immutable scalar facts.
A single native ProgramPhaseSchedule runs each inserted phase; the original phase schedule is immutable typed parent data on that owning Hongji receipt, without a second mutable pending object.
All card movement, equipment replacement, movement/health/damage/rescue children, checkpoint restoration and per-view prompt projection use native boundaries.

Multiple Hongji promises frozen in one native phase-ending window remain reserved on that exact typed parent while an earlier sibling inserts a phase. A nested child ending cannot consume the original later sibling; no use-ID or pending reservation sidecar is added.
